mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the prior 3 months compresses discount rates for equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate lower borrowing costs and increased liquidity.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >60% of periods with FEDFUNDS decline over 3 months, or Rank IC <0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained unemployment rate rise above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering immediate negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC <0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) for three consecutive months signal broad-based demand contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as recession risks escalate.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >60% of periods with joint HOUST/RSAFS declines, or interaction term Rank IC <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS >4.5%), a concurrent CPI rise above 3.5% signals persistent inflation, prompting sustained high rates that depress equity valuations and cause negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of triggered periods, or joint condition Rank IC <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A two-month consecutive decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 signals manufacturing contraction, triggering immediate negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days as supply chain disruptions reduce corporate output.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC <0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) supports consumer spending growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings strengthen.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >60% of periods with PAYEMS growth, or Rank IC <0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansions (GDPC1 annual growth >2.5%), a two-month consecutive decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals housing market weakness, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days as demand shocks spread.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 annual growth > 2.5% and HOUST decline for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >60% of triggered periods, or joint condition Rank IC <0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A three-month consecutive decline in consumer spending (RSAFS) below its 12-month moving average signals weakening retail demand, triggering negative S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days as corporate revenue expectations fall.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS < 12-month moving average for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >60% of triggered instances, or Rank IC <0.03 over 3-year windows.
